record.paper_title: Models, feedback control, and open problems of 3D bipedal robotic walking
record.original_question: Develop new cost functions for controller design in bipedal robots that go beyond integral-squared torque per step length and specific cost of transport, using a notion of distance from human-like walking. The objective is to obtain optimization criteria whose minimizers produce periodic gaits that are closer to human walking and therefore potentially more transferable to prosthetic devices.

evidence.quote: Once a viable metric for comparing walking gaits has been found, it can be used to develop new cost-functions.

Yet, currently, there are only two cost functions that are typically considered: the integral-squared torque per step length (as was considered in this paper, see (70)) and the specific cost of transport.
it may be possible to develop better cost functions, i.e., cost functions such that, when minimized, yield periodic solutions that are very “close” to human-like walking gaits.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction in bipedal locomotion control. Subsequent literature on human-inspired control and human-like cost functions exists (e.g., human-inspired hybrid zero dynamics, learning-based imitation cost designs), but no canonical resolution providing a universal metric d and a provably superior cost functional has been established. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: Human-Inspired Control of Bipedal Walking Robots
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces human-inspired cost functions based on fitting human data; ongoing area of research.
status_evidence.claim: Research on human-like cost functions for bipedal walking continues; no definitive metric/cost has been universally adopted.
